title: The Donkey and the Monkey
summary: Seeing a trained monkey receive walnuts for dancing on a rope, the donkey tried to hop and dance on its hind legs before Nasruddin's porch, smashing three flowerpots....
full_text:
Beneath the shade of the grand mulberry tree in the village square, where the townsfolk gathered to escape the midday heat and exchange gossip, Mulla Nasruddin found himself in the middle of a curious scene. Seeing a trained monkey receive walnuts for dancing on a rope, the donkey tried to hop and dance on its hind legs before Nasruddin's porch, smashing three flowerpots..... The local folk, who never missed an opportunity to hear the Mulla’s unexpected pronouncements, quickly formed an expectant circle around him, stroking their beards and whispering among themselves.

Seeing everyone staring at him with grave expressions, Nasruddin adjusted his voluminous turban with theatrical dignity. A crowd of curious onlookers gathered in a circle, eagerly anticipating how the Mulla would resolve the impossible dilemma. Rather than offering a conventional, boring answer that any dry scholar might recite, the Mulla approached the problem from an angle that no one in the village had ever dreamed possible.

With effortless timing and a completely straight face, Nasruddin delivered his masterstroke: With deadpan gravity and a twinkle in his eye, Nasruddin delivered his unforgettable verdict.  The entire square erupted into bewildered chuckles and hearty laughter, leaving the bewildered questioners shaking their heads in admiration, proving that mimicking antics that are foreign to your nature makes you look ridiculous.
moral: Mimicking antics that are foreign to your nature makes you look ridiculous.
